# Proxy nodes published in public v2ray/xray subscription lists, shaped to the
# throttle tier for LOW-TRUST POOL DEVICES ONLY. Nothing here affects any other
# device, and that scope is what makes a list this size defensible: it is
# machine generated from someone else's file, it is far too large to check
# address by address, and a mistake in it therefore must not be able to reach
# the whole house. custom-throttle-list.txt is the house-wide file and is
# curated by hand precisely because it is.
#
# The scope is enforced in forward_throttle in ip-blocklist.nix, on the
# conntrack sentinel that qos-mark stamps for pool devices — not on the pool
# MAC set, which would only ever match the upload direction.
#
# One address per line, `#` comments. Parsed at build time, so a typo fails the
# rebuild.
#
# THIS FILE HAS TWO SECTIONS SINCE 2026-09-02 AND THEY ARE MAINTAINED
# DIFFERENTLY. The first is generated by ./fetch-v2ray-nodes.py, which documents
# every filter and why it is there, and is replaced wholesale by it — do not
# hand-edit an entry there, because the next run will not know about it. The
# second, below the PSIPHON banner at the end, comes from
# ./fetch-psiphon-servers.py, and that script does not write this file.
#
# SO A REGENERATION IS A REPLACEMENT OF THE FIRST SECTION ONLY. Redirecting the
# v2ray script over this file discards the Psiphon block and this header without
# a word, and the build then succeeds on the smaller file, so nothing downstream
# will tell you it happened. Splice instead:
#
#   ./fetch-v2ray-nodes.py > /tmp/v2ray.txt
#   # keep everything up to the generated-block marker, substitute /tmp/v2ray.txt
#   # for the addresses above the PSIPHON banner, keep the banner and its block
#
# PROVENANCE, AND ITS LIMIT. Every address below was PUBLISHED as a proxy
# endpoint in a public subscription file. That is a much stronger claim than
# "a device talked to it" — the operator is asserting it is a node. It is NOT
# the same as a checked address: these have not been probed, and no PTR or
# certificate was read for the great majority. Nothing here should be quoted as
# a confirmed tunnel; it is intel, and it is a snapshot of a list that upstream
# rewrites every few minutes.
#
# WHY A THROTTLE AND NOT A BLOCK. A blocked node fails cleanly, and the clients
# these lists serve score candidate nodes and discard the ones that fail — so
# blocking teaches the client to move on, which is the outcome this file exists
# to prevent. A bare bitrate cap is near-invisible to that scoring: probes pass
# under it, the node keeps measuring healthy and stays selected, and anything
# carrying real data crawls. Same reasoning as custom-throttle-list.txt.
#
# WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY THROWN AWAY. About a quarter of the published endpoints
# are CDN addresses and are excluded, because with SNI-routed fronting a client
# can dial ANY edge address and carry the real host in the SNI and the Host
# header. The address identifies nothing, and shaping it degrades whatever else
# the house reaches through that edge. Three independent guards do this, and
# each caught something the others missed — see the script's docstring for the
# worked examples, of which 1.1.1.1 and 127.0.0.1 are the two worth knowing.
#
# DOMAINS ARE NOT USED. The source also carries 854 domain endpoints. They are
# left out on purpose: most resolve into CDN space that is excluded here
# anyway, an answer resolved from this network is ISP-steered and not what the
# node's own users get, and a domain's address today is not its address next
# week. If they are ever wanted they belong in a DNS list, not this one.
#
# AMAZON IS PRESENT, MICROSOFT IS NOT. Both ASNs carry tenant compute and the
# provider's own CDN edge, so the AS number cannot separate them. Reverse DNS
# can, for Amazon: an EC2 tenant resolves to *.compute.amazonaws.com and a
# CloudFront edge does not. Azure VMs get no PTR, so the same test says nothing
# about the 21 Microsoft addresses and they are dropped unchecked.
#
# THE PREVIOUS VERSION OF THIS PARAGRAPH WAS WRONG BY 2026-08-30, and how it
# went wrong is the useful part. It said all 126 Amazon addresses resolved to
# *.compute.amazonaws.com with "no CloudFront among them" — true when checked
# by hand on the first run, and stated as though it were a property of Amazon
# rather than a fact about one day's list. This run kept 108 Amazon addresses
# and 18.239.134.69 among them reverse-resolved to
# server-18-239-134-69.bkk50.r.cloudfront.net: a shared CDN edge, in the one
# file whose founding argument is that shaping a shared edge degrades the whole
# house. 198.211.4.60 was the second reject, on a junk PTR
# (undefined.hostname.localhost) that proves nothing either way.
#
# The check is therefore no longer a manual one. fetch-v2ray-nodes.py runs it
# as filter 7 on every Amazon address, every run, and refuses to produce output
# at all if the resolver looks broken — a resolver that is down would reject
# all 108 and read exactly like a list with no EC2 nodes in it.
#
# Generated 2026-08-30 from Epodonios/v2ray-configs All_Configs_Sub.txt.
# 2051 unique IP endpoints in the source, 552 rejected by the filters.
# ADDRESSES BELOW THIS LINE ARE GENERATED, AS FAR AS THE PSIPHON BANNER at the
# end of the file — which is not generated by that script and must survive a
# regeneration. See the header before editing.

# ############################################################################
# PSIPHON — NOT GENERATED BY fetch-v2ray-nodes.py. PRESERVE ON REGENERATION.
# ############################################################################
#
# 415 addresses from Psiphon's LIVE remote server list, fetched and verified on
# 2026-09-02 with ./fetch-psiphon-servers.py. Placed here on the operator's
# instruction, having been offered for custom-ip-blocklist.txt where the
# existing Psiphon estate lives.
#
# HOW THEY WERE ESTABLISHED, in order:
#   * fetched from s3.amazonaws.com/psiphon/web/iohq-waa4-q4dt/server_list_compressed,
#     public and unauthenticated, the same URL the client uses;
#   * the RSA-4096 signature over the payload VERIFIED against the
#     RemoteServerListSignaturePublicKey pinned in the script, and the signing
#     key digest matched — the script prints nothing if either check fails;
#   * 483 entries decoded, 38 already in the router's lists, 445 new. All 445
#     were then re-checked by CIDR CONTAINMENT against custom-throttle-list.txt,
#     custom-ip-blocklist.txt and this file, because the script's own dedupe is
#     exact string match and those files are mostly prefixes now. Nothing was
#     already covered;
#   * PROBED FROM THE ROUTER, each node on the ports its own record declares:
#     415 answered, 30 did not and are omitted.
#
# THE PROBE HAD TO RUN ON THE ROUTER and that is not a detail. The shaper hooks
# forward, so an address already being shaped reads as dead from a LAN client
# and would have been dropped from this list for the wrong reason.
#
# STRONGER PROVENANCE THAN THE GENERATED BLOCK ABOVE. Those addresses were
# published in someone's subscription file and never touched. These were signed
# by Psiphon as its own current estate and then answered a connection on a port
# they themselves advertised. The header's "it is intel, not evidence" caveat is
# aimed at the generated section; it understates these.
#
# MOST OF THIS BLOCK CHANGES NOTHING TODAY, AND THAT IS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE
# ANYONE QUOTES ITS SIZE. This file is POOL-ONLY, and 396 of the 415 already sit
# inside an AS in custom-lowtrust-asns.txt, which DROPS them for pool devices.
# A dropped packet never reaches the shaper, so for those 396 the row below is
# inert — belt and braces against an ASN later being removed from that list, and
# nothing more. The count is against ip2asn-combined.tsv, the checked-in table
# the build actually expands that list from, not the router's live one.
#
# THE 19 THAT DO ADD COVERAGE are the whole practical effect of this block:
#   13  AS31898  Oracle (OCI) — not in custom-lowtrust-asns.txt
#    5  unplaced in ip2asn-combined.tsv, so no ASN entry can reach them
#    1  AS58065  PacketExchange
# They are marked <-- below.
#
# THREE OF THOSE 19 ARE 108.165.21.160, .208 AND .222, and they are a warning
# about reading the 2026-08-28 note in custom-ip-blocklist.txt too quickly. It
# says the 9 addresses not covered by an ASN fell "inside 108.165.21.0/24",
# which reads as though that /24 were listed. It is not: that file carries nine
# individual /32s in it (.53 .105 .116 .132 .155 .174 .190 .238 .241) and no
# prefix. The sentence described where the addresses clustered, not what was
# entered. Every address in this block was checked by containment for that
# reason, and these three sit in the same /24 while being covered by nothing.
#
# WHERE THE REST OF THE ESTATE IS: 1,169 older Psiphon addresses are in
# custom-ip-blocklist.txt as LAN-WIDE DROPS, moved there on 2026-08-28. So the
# estate is now split across two files with two scopes AND two treatments —
# dropped for every device there, shaped for pool devices only here. That is a
# deliberate instruction, not drift, but it means "is this Psiphon node covered"
# has no single answer any more and both files must be checked.
#
# EXPECT ROTATION TO OUTRUN THIS. 445 of 483 entries were new against lists
# refreshed on 2026-08-28 — a ~92% turnover in five days, matching the ~93%
# the 2026-08-28 note recorded. Refresh rather than accumulate:
#   modules/router/fetch-psiphon-servers.py --new --probe
# Run it on the router. --json-raw carries live ssh passwords and host keys and
# this repository is public, so never commit that output.
